hook.line: When you have made your point, a good speaker adds the one thing that keeps it honest. Without it, a text reads like a leaflet.
hook.es: Dicho esto, la propuesta tiene cosas buenas.
hook.en: That said, the proposal has some good points.

examples.es: Dicho esto, la propuesta tiene cosas buenas.
examples.en: That said, the proposal has some good points.

examples.es: Ahora bien, el costo es muy alto.
examples.en: Having said that, the cost is very high.

examples.es: Dicho esto, habría que hablar con los vecinos.
examples.en: That said, we would need to talk to the neighbours.

examples.es: Ahora bien, no todos piensan igual.
examples.en: Having said that, not everyone thinks alike.

examples.es: Dicho esto, habría que pensarlo bien.
examples.en: That said, we would need to think it through.

rule:
Make your main point first. Then add your reservation with *Dicho esto, …* (that said) or *Ahora bien, …* (having said that).

Both go at the start of the new sentence, followed by a comma. Nothing changes in the verbs.

To say what would need doing, use *habría que* plus an infinitive: *habría que pensarlo bien*.

This is the voice of a meeting, a debate or an essay. With friends you would just say *pero*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these discourse markers: small phrases that signal where an argument is turning.

readAndPick.es: Dicho esto, la propuesta tiene cosas buenas.
options: That said, the proposal has some good points.
The proposal says it has good points.
That said, the proposal has no good points.

readAndPick.es: Ahora bien, el costo es muy alto.
options: Having said that, the cost is very high.
Now, the cost is very high.
The cost is very high now.

readAndPick.es: Dicho esto, habría que hablar con los vecinos.
options: The neighbours said we should talk.
That said, we would need to talk to the neighbours.
That said, I talked to the neighbours.

readAndPick.es: Ahora bien, no todos piensan igual.
options: Having said that, not everyone thinks alike.
Having said that, everyone thinks alike.
Not everyone thinks now.

readAndPick.es: Dicho esto, habría que pensarlo bien.
options: That said, we would need to think it through.
That said, I thought it through.
That said, there is no need to think.

readAndPick.es: Ahora bien, Vale no está de acuerdo.
options: Having said that, Vale doesn't agree.
Vale says she agrees now.
Having said that, Vale agrees.

readAndPick.es: Dicho esto, el barrio necesita un cambio.
options: That said, the neighbourhood needs a change.
The neighbourhood needs a change, which I have said.
The neighbourhood has said it needs a change.

readAndPick.es: Ahora bien, el proyecto tiene un problema.
options: Now the project has a problem, so I said so.
Having said that, the project has a problem.
The project has a problem now.

yourTurn.prompt: Type the whole sentence, choosing *habría que* or *habría*: Dicho esto, ___ pensarlo bien.
yourTurn.answer: Dicho esto, habría que pensarlo bien.
yourTurn.why: The frame is *habría que* plus an infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it: "That said, the proposal has some good points."
yourTurn.answer: Dicho esto, la propuesta tiene cosas buenas.
accept: Dicho eso, la propuesta tiene cosas buenas.
yourTurn.why: *Dicho esto* opens the reservation and takes a comma.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it: "Having said that, the cost is very high."
yourTurn.answer: Ahora bien, el costo es muy alto.
yourTurn.why: *Ahora bien* is the other way to open the reservation.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it: "Having said that, not everyone thinks alike."
yourTurn.answer: Ahora bien, no todos piensan igual.
yourTurn.why: The verb does not change after *ahora bien*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it: "That said, we would need to talk to the neighbours."
yourTurn.answer: Dicho esto, habría que hablar con los vecinos.
accept: Ahora bien, habría que hablar con los vecinos.
yourTurn.why: *Habría que* plus an infinitive says what would need to be done.

yourTurn.prompt: Say both sentences: "The square is important. That said, the project has a problem."
yourTurn.answer: La plaza es importante. Dicho esto, el proyecto tiene un problema.
accept: La plaza es importante. Ahora bien, el proyecto tiene un problema.
yourTurn.why: The main point comes first and the reservation follows.

yourTurn.prompt: Swap the opener for the other one: Dicho esto, el barrio necesita un cambio.
yourTurn.answer: Ahora bien, el barrio necesita un cambio.
yourTurn.why: *Ahora bien* and *dicho esto* do the same job here.

pitfalls.wrong: Dicho esto que la propuesta tiene cosas buenas.
pitfalls.right: Dicho esto, la propuesta tiene cosas buenas.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Dicho esto* is a separate opener, so it takes a comma and no *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Ahora, el costo es muy alto.
pitfalls.right: Ahora bien, el costo es muy alto.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Ahora* alone means "now"; you need *bien* to get "having said that".

pitfalls.wrong: Después de decir esto, la propuesta tiene cosas buenas.
pitfalls.right: Dicho esto, la propuesta tiene cosas buenas.
pitfalls.why: A word-for-word "after saying this" is clumsy; *dicho esto* is the short form people use.

personal: Say one thing you like about your town or neighbourhood. Then add a reservation with *Dicho esto, …* or *Ahora bien, …*.
